_comment: Local models PrepBench can recommend. Data, not code, so the list can be
updated without a release and a user can edit it for their own hardware.
'licence' is shown in the picker on purpose. It decides whether a model
could ever be bundled with a paid product, and that is far cheaper to
know when choosing than to discover later. Apache-2.0 entries are the
'ram_required_gb' is the free memory the model needs at the stated context
size, not the download size. It is the number that decides whether this
will work at all, so recommendations are ranked by it.
PrepBench never downloads any of these. The URL is shown to the user, who

models.label: Qwen2.5 1.5B Instruct (Q4_K_M)
models.summary: Runs almost anywhere. Fine for generating practice questions; too small to grade a system design answer well.

models.label: Qwen2.5 3B Instruct (Q4_K_M)
models.summary: A step up in writing quality. Note the licence is research-only, unlike the other Qwen sizes here.

models.label: Qwen2.5 7B Instruct (Q4_K_M)
models.summary: The sweet spot. Grades system design answers usefully, though a good deal slower than a cloud model.

models.label: Mistral 7B Instruct v0.3 (Q4_K_M)
models.summary: Comparable to Qwen 7B and a little lighter. Worth trying if Qwen feels slow.

models.label: Qwen2.5 14B Instruct (Q4_K_M)
models.summary: The closest you will get to cloud-quality feedback locally. Wants a lot of memory and is slow on CPU alone.

ollama.label: Ollama

Open a terminal and pull a model with the command below.

llamafile.label: Llamafile
llamafile.summary: A single executable, no installer, and it runs from a USB stick. Best when you cannot install software.

windows: Download llamafile.exe from the releases page.
Download a .gguf model file from the model's page.
Put both in the same folder, then start the server with the command below.
Leave that window open while you use PrepBench.
macos: Download the llamafile binary from the releases page.
Download a .gguf model file from the model's page.
Start the server with the command below and leave it running.
linux: Download the llamafile binary from the releases page.
Download a .gguf model file from the model's page.
Start the server with the command below and leave it running.

lmstudio.label: LM Studio
lmstudio.summary: A desktop app with a model browser built in. Good if you would rather click than type.

windows: Search for a model in its Discover tab and download it.
Open the Developer / Local Server tab and press Start Server.
macos: Search for a model in its Discover tab and download it.
Open the Developer / Local Server tab and press Start Server.
linux: Download the LM Studio AppImage and make it executable.
Search for a model in its Discover tab and download it.
Open the Developer / Local Server tab and press Start Server.
